sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Theme toggle button styles
sections.what: Styles the button that switches between light and dark themes, in both themes. It sets the button to at least 44 pixels so it is easy to tap, and gives it a thin outline that changes on hover.
sections.why: Likely reason: 44 pixels is a common minimum size for touch targets.

sections.name: html[data-theme="dark"]  (part 1)
sections.title: Dark colour palette and font choices
sections.what: Defines the dark theme's named colours and fonts, such as near-black backgrounds, warm off-white text, icy blue and cyan data colours, champagne for verified evidence, and coral for accents. It then points the app's existing colour names at these values, so most of the interface switches when dark mode is on.
sections.why: The header comment says the dark layer is a separate palette that leaves the light design untouched.
sections.watch_out: Many other dark rules read these named colours, so changing one value shifts the look of the whole app.

sections.name: html[data-theme="dark"]  (part 2)
sections.title: Remapping app colour names for dark mode
sections.what: Maps the app's shared colour names for surfaces, text, buttons, sidebars, inputs and the browser's own form controls to dark values. It also sets the page to dark mode so scrollbars and native controls follow.
sections.why: The comment explains that elements which used white text on dark surfaces are flipped, so the text stays readable.
sections.watch_out: Code that uses the plain white or black colour names gets the opposite of what it expects in dark mode.

sections.name: html[data-theme="dark"] body
sections.title: Body, buttons, headers and hero in dark
sections.what: Sets the dark page background, body font, selected-text highlight, and dark panels. It styles the primary button as off-white with dark text, the editorial headings and labels, the top header, and the front hero section, whose photo is replaced by a code-built plant.
sections.why: The hero comment says the code-built plant replaces the photograph. The reason for the other choices is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The hero content turns off mouse and touch input, and only links and buttons get it back, so any other clickable element placed there will not respond.

sections.name: html[data-theme="dark"] .cpi-dotmatrix
sections.title: Dot-matrix photos, tiles and workspace chrome
sections.what: Turns photos into a grayscale dot-matrix look using a pattern mask, adjusts tool tile colours and photo caption text, and sets dark backgrounds for workspaces. It also gives the yard header a coral top edge and inverts the logo so it shows in dark mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: bright photos would stand out too much against dark backgrounds, so they are toned down.
sections.watch_out: The logo is found by its file name, so renaming the logo file would stop the inversion without any error.

sections.name: html[data-theme="dark"] .house-shimmer-text
sections.title: Charts, maps and input fields in dark
sections.what: Restyles the shimmer text effect, chart grids, axis labels and tooltips, and the map so it reads on dark. It also sets input fields and placeholder text to dark-friendly colours.
sections.why: The comment says charts are inline graphics that need explicit dark colours to stay readable.
sections.watch_out: The map is recoloured with a filter rather than a dark map style, so its colours are only approximate.

sections.name: html[data-theme="dark"] .cpi-paper-island  (part 1)
sections.title: Paper island keeps slides light
sections.what: Inside any element marked as the paper island, the app switches back to the light palette, so slides, decks and exports look like the standard design. Chart text inside it is also set to light values.
sections.why: The header comment says slides and decks stay light because they are house output.
sections.watch_out: Any element that should stay light must sit inside the paper island marker, or it will render dark.

sections.name: html[data-theme="dark"] .cpi-paper-island  (part 2)
sections.title: Animated build panel and its status chrome
sections.what: Styles the dark animated build panel, which the file calls a collation field. This covers its caption, top bar, progress list with done, active and failed states, legend, chips, tooltip and status labels. On screens narrower than 760 pixels, the progress list and legend are hidden.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for leaving these rules outside the dark theme marker.
sections.watch_out: These rules are not limited to dark mode, so they also apply in light mode, and any new progress state needs its own rule to be coloured.

summary: Dark-mode style rules that recolour the app only when the dark theme is on, while keeping slides and exports light.
purpose: Gives the app a dark look without changing the default light design.
why: The header comment says the light design is the default and is not touched. Every rule is limited to the dark theme marker.
how: Defines the dark palette and fonts, then points the app's shared colour names at dark values. It then restyles the hero, photos, workspaces, charts, inputs and a light panel type for slides. Last, it styles the animated build panel and its status states.
inputs: The dark theme marker on the page root, and the class names used by app components.
outputs: Colours, fonts and small layout changes that show only in dark mode, plus the light paper panels.
risks: Most rules apply only in dark mode, but the final build panel rules are not limited to dark mode, so they also show in light mode. Some colours are fixed values rather than named values, so changing the palette will not change them. Fonts named here must be loaded elsewhere, since this file does not load them. Some variables used here are defined in other files.
debug: If a page looks light in dark mode, check that the page root has the dark theme marker. If a colour is wrong, check whether it comes from a named value or a fixed value. Slides staying light is intended. If a build panel looks wrong in light mode, that is the unlimited rules. Look in other style files for any missing variable.
